inputs.text: Tens of thousands marched in central London with trade unions, anti-racism groups and Muslim representative bodies—people standing together against far-right politics and the harm it can do to vulnerable communities. Calling that an attempt to silence voters turns collective action into a threat without showing that anyone’s debate is being shut down. People deserve to discuss social and economic concerns, but “open debate” cannot mean giving prejudice a free pass or asking targeted communities to accept it in the name of tradition. The answer is to confront the inequalities and insecurity that fuel division, not to dismiss anti-racist organising as an effort to police opinion.
